top.text: When opponents drop, wherever it lands, Chochuwong loses the point within two shots 18% of the time (n=202, 95% CI 14%-24%); typical pros lose 10% after the same shot (difference +9 points, 95% CI +4 to +14, n=7118).

When opponents drop to Chochuwong's front forehand, Chochuwong loses the point within two shots 22% of the time (n=59, 95% CI 13%-34%); typical pros lose 10% after the same shot (difference +12 points, 95% CI +3 to +24, n=1465).

When Chochuwong plays a defensive return to the opponent's front forehand, Chochuwong loses the point within two shots 22% of the time (n=41, 95% CI 12%-37%); typical pros lose 11% after the same shot (difference +11 points, 95% CI +1 to +26, n=2436).

When Chochuwong lobs to the opponent's rear forehand, Chochuwong loses the point within two shots 16% of the time (n=83, 95% CI 9%-25%); typical pros lose 9% after the same shot (difference +6 points, 95% CI 0 to +16, n=5260).

xp.caveat: Read this first: xP from shot and position data has no signal mid-rally in elite singles (holdout AUC 0.50 on strokes that did not end the rally). The same features reach AUC 0.79 only on final strokes, where the task is classifying how an already-decisive stroke ends (winner or error), not predicting a rally. Nothing in this section is a working expected-points model.
